english_text: An interactive beginner course in Modern Standard Arabic: learn all 28 letters and how they connect, the short-vowel marks, vocabulary by topic and simple sentences, with a daily spaced-repetition review and typing practice. Free, no account, and your progress stays on your device.
What you will learn

The course follows a clear beginner path: 1. the 28 letters, their names, sounds and shapes; 2. harakat (fatha, kasra, damma, sukun, shadda, tanween); 3. reading and typing from single letters up to short sentences, using the on-screen Arabic keyboard; 4. starter vocabulary (numbers, colours, family, greetings) and everyday vocabulary (food, home, daily routines, clothing, time, places, travel, shopping, weather, school and work); 5. sentence patterns such as “This is a …” and “Where is …?”; 6. eight practical conversations; 7. reading comprehension, from short sentences to beginner stories. Each letter lesson ends with a short check, and a lesson is marked complete only when you pass it.
priority_reason: explains joining rules and dialect scope to learners

english_text: How Arabic letters connect

arabic_as_implemented: ا د ذ ر ز و  |  دار
english_text: Arabic is written right to left, and most letters join to the next one, changing shape by position: alone, at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end of a connected group. Six letters never join to the letter after them: ا د ذ ر ز و. After one of these the next letter starts a fresh shape, which is why words such as دار (daar, “house”) look broken into pieces.
priority_reason: explains joining rules and dialect scope to learners

english_text: Daily review

Each time you answer a question about a letter, a word or a sentence, the course records the result for that item and schedules its next review. A correct answer moves the item to a longer interval; a miss brings it back tomorrow. Open the daily review to practise whatever is due. Your progress and review schedule are saved on your device only, with no account.
